explain.say: Most sand starts as solid rock in mountains. Ice, rain, heat and plant roots crack it into smaller and smaller pieces, a process called weathering.

explain.say: Rivers carry the pieces downhill. As they tumble and knock together, the sharp corners wear off and the grains become smaller and rounder.

explain.say: Softer minerals break down and wash away, leaving tough grains, mostly quartz. A grain counts as sand if it is between about one sixteenth of a millimetre and two millimetres across.
Finally waves and wind pile sand into beaches and dunes. Some beaches are different: white sand on tropical islands can be broken coral and shells, and black sand comes from volcanic rock.

faq.a: Most sand is grains of quartz, a hard mineral that lasts after softer minerals wear away. Some sand is made of broken shells and coral, or of dark volcanic rock.
As rivers, waves and wind move the grains, they bump and rub against each other, wearing off sharp corners. The longer they travel, the rounder they become.

faq.q: Why is some sand white and some black?
faq.a: White tropical sand is often crushed coral and shells. Black sand comes from dark volcanic rock like basalt, as on beaches in Hawaii and Iceland. Golden sand is mostly quartz stained by iron.

faq.q: How big is a grain of sand?
faq.a: Geologists call a grain sand if it is between about 0.06 and 2 millimetres across. Smaller grains are silt and clay; bigger ones are granules and pebbles.

faq.q: How long does it take to make sand?
faq.a: Often thousands to millions of years. Some quartz grains have been recycled through several rock cycles over hundreds of millions of years.

facts: Quartz is the most common mineral in most beach and desert sand.
Geologists define sand as grains between 0.0625 and 2 millimetres across.

quiz.say: Why is quartz the most common mineral in sand?
quiz.show: Quartz is common in sand because…

options.show: It is hard and does not break down easily
options.say: It is hard and does not break down easily

quiz.why: Quartz is hard and resists weathering, so it is left behind while softer minerals wear away.

wrong.1: Some sand is made by sea creatures, but quartz comes from rock.
wrong.2: Quartz is hard, 7 on the Mohs scale, not soft.
